question: My Canadian passport was stolen while I was abroad. Which Canadian office should I contact first?
generated_answer:
You should contact the nearest Canadian embassy, high commission or consulate general. In some countries, there may be more than one Canadian office, so you should contact the office that is responsible for the country where you are currently located. You can find the contact information for all Canadian embassies, high commissions and consulates general on the Government of Canada's website at https://travel.gc.ca/assistance/embassies. You should also report the theft of your passport to the local police, and obtain a police report, as you will need this to apply for a new passport.

It is important to act quickly to report the loss or theft of your passport, as it may be used for fraudulent purposes if it falls into the wrong hands. In addition to reporting the loss or theft of your passport, you should also contact your credit card companies and bank to inform them of the theft and to cancel any cards that may have been in your passport.

If you are in a situation where you need to travel immediately and do not have time to apply for a new passport, you may be able to obtain an emergency travel document (also known as an "ETD") from the nearest Canadian embassy, high commission or consulate general. An ETD is a temporary document that can be used to travel to Canada, and it is usually issued on the same day that you apply for it. However, an ETD is not a full passport and may not be accepted by all countries or airlines, so it is best to try to obtain a new passport as soon as possible.

In summary, if your Canadian passport is stolen while you are abroad, you should contact the nearest Canadian embassy, high commission or consulate general to report the loss or theft and to apply for a new passport or an emergency travel document, as well as to report the theft to the local police and to contact your credit card companies and bank to inform them of the theft and to cancel any cards that may have been in your passport.
